journeys.content_focus: Cell identity, nucleus, ribosomes, endomembrane flow, recycling/storage, and cytoskeleton
journeys.setting_logic: A coherent operations complex supports physical movement from information control to protein production, processing, recycling, storage, and internal structural support.

journeys.premise: A living-cell operations complex has suffered a routing failure. Protein cargo is being sent to the wrong places, damaged material is accumulating, and the internal support network is destabilizing.
journeys.mission: Enter through cell identity control, trace information and protein handling from nucleus to ribosome to ER to Golgi, then restore recycling, storage, oxidation, and cytoskeletal support.
journeys.stakes: If the routes remain confused, the learner cannot explain how organelle structure produces cell function.
journeys.continuity_object: a single red protein-cargo case that begins as an mRNA-directed product and is followed through the endomembrane route
journeys.opening_image: A transparent building shaped like a eukaryotic cell flickers above Nia’s tablet; several internal routes are flashing red.
journeys.ending_payoff: The red cargo case reaches its destination, damaged components are recycled, reservoirs stabilize, and the cytoskeletal rails relight across the complex.
journeys.tone: investigative, concrete, lightly suspenseful, never frantic
narrative_constraints: The learner always knows where they are relative to the previous locus.

journeys.setting_logic: A power-conversion annex makes nested membranes, compartments, surface area, and energy-conversion structures spatially explicit without mixing them into the already dense endomembrane route.

journeys.premise: The complex has power, but the output is unstable. Nia takes the learner into two transparent energy-conversion chambers to inspect exactly where membrane geometry supports cellular energy transformations.
journeys.mission: Map mitochondrial compartments and cristae, compare energy demand with mitochondrial abundance, then inspect chloroplast membranes, thylakoids, grana, stroma, and chlorophyll.
journeys.stakes: The learner must distinguish the two organelles by internal architecture and location of major processes, not by vague “powerhouse” or “photosynthesis organelle” slogans.
journeys.continuity_object: a pulsing energy-demand meter that changes as the learner moves between cell types and organelles
journeys.opening_image: Two enormous transparent organelles sit behind glass like working power plants, one orange and folded within, one green and stacked within.
journeys.ending_payoff: The demand meter stabilizes after the learner correctly routes each process to the membrane or compartment that supports it.

journeys.content_focus: Surface-area-to-volume relationships, cell-size constraints, exchange surfaces, and organism scaling
journeys.setting_logic: A modeling observatory lets learners compare geometrically similar objects at different scales and watch exchange and thermal consequences change with size.

journeys.premise: An observatory has enlarged a cell model until its interior is starving even though the outer surface looks enormous.
journeys.mission: Use geometric models to discover why surface area and volume scale differently, then restore exchange by changing shape and compare thermal consequences across organism sizes.
journeys.stakes: The learner must see why “bigger” does not mean proportionally more exchange surface.
journeys.continuity_object: a glowing exchange meter that turns from green to red as model size increases and back toward green when surface folds are added
journeys.opening_image: A tiny cube cell glows bright green beside an enormous identical cube whose center is dim and oxygen-starved.
journeys.ending_payoff: The giant model regains exchange capacity after the learner adds surface folds and explains the scaling rule.
journeys.tone: discovery-driven, visual, mathematical without feeling like a worksheet

journeys.content_focus: Membrane structure, fluidity, proteins, recognition, selective permeability, cell walls, and plasmodesmata
journeys.setting_logic: A border terminal gives the membrane one stable spatial metaphor: a dynamic boundary with a molecular fabric, embedded workers, recognition markers, selective lanes, and an external plant-cell wall.

journeys.premise: A molecular border terminal is admitting the wrong travelers. Nia freezes the terminal so the learner can inspect the membrane fabric, embedded proteins, identity tags, and outer plant-cell wall.
journeys.mission: Rebuild the bilayer orientation, restore fluidity, place membrane proteins correctly, distinguish recognition markers, and reopen selective passage lanes.
journeys.stakes: The learner must understand that selectivity comes from molecular properties and membrane structure, not from a membrane “deciding” what it wants.
journeys.continuity_object: a tray of test travelers—O2, CO2, H2O, NH3, glucose, Na+, and K+—used at successive checkpoints
journeys.opening_image: A flexible two-layer border ripples under bright lights while a line of differently shaped molecules waits for entry.
journeys.ending_payoff: Each traveler reaches the correct lane and the neighboring plant-cell wall reconnects through a plasmodesma.
journeys.tone: busy border-terminal mystery with clear molecular rules

journeys.content_focus: Diffusion, passive/active transport, facilitated diffusion, channels/carriers, bulk transport, electrochemical gradients, pumps, and cotransport
journeys.setting_logic: A multilevel transit hub makes direction, gradients, energy use, transport proteins, vesicles, and coupled movement visible as different ways of crossing the same boundary.

journeys.premise: The transport hub has lost its direction signs. Molecules are moving randomly, pumps are stalled, and vesicle docks are jammed.
journeys.mission: Reconstruct concentration gradients, passive and active transport, facilitated diffusion, channels, carriers, aquaporins, vesicle transport, membrane potential, electrogenic pumps, and cotransport.
journeys.stakes: The learner must track direction, energy use, and the transport structure used in each case.
journeys.continuity_object: a set of colored cargo tokens whose position and energy tags are followed across every transport system
journeys.opening_image: A sloped concourse is crowded on one side and almost empty on the other; powered lifts and membrane gates stand dark.
journeys.ending_payoff: The hub runs again with downhill lanes, ATP-powered routes, vesicle docks, and coupled transport all moving in their correct directions.
journeys.tone: kinetic and mechanical, with strong directional logic

journeys.content_focus: Tonicity, osmosis, water potential, plant-cell water responses, and osmoregulation
journeys.setting_logic: A glass conservatory with controlled solution chambers makes water movement and plant-cell responses visible while separating conceptual tonicity from quantitative water-potential work.

journeys.premise: A glass conservatory contains living cells in solution chambers. Several are swelling, shrinking, or losing contact with their walls because the solution controls have been mixed up.
journeys.mission: Diagnose tonicity, observe isotonic/hypertonic/hypotonic outcomes, then use water potential and osmoregulation controls to explain water movement quantitatively and conceptually.
journeys.stakes: The learner must distinguish solution labels from the direction of water movement and understand why plant and animal cells respond differently.
journeys.continuity_object: one transparent reference cell and one plant cell that reappear in each solution chamber
journeys.opening_image: Three glass rooms fog with condensation while one cell shrinks, another swells, and a plant cell presses hard against its wall.
journeys.ending_payoff: The chambers stabilize when the learner predicts water movement from water potential and restores internal balance.
journeys.tone: calm but visually dramatic laboratory greenhouse

journeys.premise: The final archive asks two linked questions: why eukaryotic cells divide chemistry into internal compartments, and where mitochondria and chloroplasts came from.
journeys.mission: Demonstrate the advantages of compartmentalization, compare prokaryotic and eukaryotic internal organization, then reconstruct endosymbiosis and examine multiple independent lines of evidence.
journeys.stakes: The learner must leave with an evidence-based evolutionary explanation, not a fantasy of organelles simply “choosing” to live inside cells.
journeys.continuity_object: an evidence case that receives one new card at each station and is sealed only when all lines of evidence agree
journeys.opening_image: Rows of archive drawers surround two illuminated cell models, one relatively open inside and one divided by internal membranes.
journeys.ending_payoff: The evidence case closes only after genomes, division, ribosomes, membranes, and modern host dependence form one coherent explanation.
journeys.tone: historical investigation grounded in visible evidence
